references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, the same expression 'to walk contrary to me' (קֶרִי) is used, showing the escalating pattern of disobedience and God's increasing punishment.
Repetition of the warning about walking contrary to God, with ensuing consequences, building up to this verse.
Moses warns of curses that will come upon Israel if they do not listen to the Lord's voice, parallel to the warning in Leviticus.
Isaiah presents the same choice between obedience and blessing or disobedience and judgment, reflecting the covenant conditions in Leviticus.
Jeremiah describes how the people did not listen to the Lord and were disobedient, fulfilling the warnings given in Leviticus 26.
Ezekiel refers to Israel's rebellion and their failure to listen to God, linking to the covenant breaches described in Leviticus.
Hebrews warns of the consequences of sinning willfully after receiving knowledge of the truth, reflecting the seriousness of persistent disobedience.
